trial_court: Senior Civil Judge/Rent Controller (East District), Karkardooma Court, Delhi in Suit RC/ARC/113/16
facts_of_case: Petitioner is landlord of shop. Respondent is tenant who shut down business and started new one without written agreement. Petitioner seeks quashing of order granting leave to defend to respondent.

legal_principles.principle: It is not for the tenant to dictate terms to the landlord as to how else he can adjust himself without getting possession of the tenanted premises.
legal_principles.held: While deciding the question of bona fides of the requirement of the landlord, it is quite unnecessary to make an endeavour as to how else the landlord could have adjusted himself.
cited_cases: Sarla Ahuja v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (1998) 8 SCC 119

legal_principles.principle: The Controller is under a statutory duty to grant leave if the affidavit filed by the tenant discloses such facts as would disentitle the landlord from obtaining an order for the recovery of possession.
legal_principles.held: Section 25-B(5) provides that the Controller is under a statutory duty -- note the expression 'shall give leave to the tenant to contest the application' to grant leave if the 'affidavit filed by the tenant discloses such facts as would disentitle the landlord from obtaining an order for the recovery of possession'.
cited_cases: Precision Steel &Engg. Works v. Prem Deva Niranjan Deva Tayal, (1982) 3 SCC 270

outcome.final_order: Order dated 05.07.2017 passed by learned Senior Civil Judge/Rent Controller (East District), Karkardooma Court, Delhi in Suit RC/ARC/113/16 is quashed.

use_for_drafting: quashing order of leave to defend
